https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=F02wGWv1ji4

值得閱讀的理由

  • 深入解析國民神飲王老吉如何從年銷200億人民幣的巔峰跌落，面臨三年內銷量縮減10億的興衰歷程。
  • 全面還原王老吉與加多寶長達十餘年的世紀商標訴訟大戰，揭示巨頭內耗如何徹底改變中國涼茶產業格局。
  • 剖析Z世代年輕族群的消費心理與無糖健康趨勢，探討傳統功能性飲料受限於特定場景的生存困境。

摘要

昔日國民神飲：從嶺南草藥到百億傳奇

作者指出，曾被譽為「國民涼茶」的王老吉在2012年年銷售額一度突破200億元人民幣，相當於全國每人每年喝掉四罐，甚至創下市場上每賣出十罐涼茶就有七罐是王老吉的驚人紀錄。回溯歷史，該品牌起源於清代道光年間廣州名醫王澤邦在街頭售賣的草藥茶，歷經歷史變遷後成為廣藥集團旗下的國有資產。真正將王老吉推向全國的關鍵人物，是後來創立加多寶集團的陳鴻道。他在1995年租賃了商標使用權，並透過定位諮詢提煉出顛覆性的廣告詞「怕上火，喝王老吉」，成功將具有嶺南地域特色的藥性飲品轉型為預防上火的功能性飲料。配合2007年豪擲4.2億元奪得央視廣告標王，王老吉銷量瞬間暴增，於2010年商標估值高達1080億元。

兩虎相爭無贏家：十餘年的世紀商標內耗

然而在王老吉如日中天之際，內部利益分配不均引爆了長達十餘年的商業大戰。作者提到，當時加多寶負責經營的紅罐王老吉年銷破百億，但身為商標擁有者的廣藥集團每年僅分得約500萬元的授權費，加上商標延期協議涉及行賄違規，雙方自2011年正式對簿公堂。整場官司圍繞三大核心展開：首先是商標歸屬，法院在2012年判決加多寶禁用王老吉商標，迫使其改名為加多寶涼茶；其次是廣告語之爭，加多寶宣傳「全國銷量領先的紅罐涼茶改名加多寶」引發訴訟，纏鬥至2019年最高法才認定其不構成虛假宣傳；最後是紅罐包裝裝潢權，最終判決雙方共享。作者分析，這場曠日持久的訴訟沒有贏家，不僅排名第三的和其正在雙雄價格戰中被邊緣化，王老吉奪回商標後銷量亦大幅腰斬，雙方皆元氣大傷。

健康風潮與場景禁錮：涼茶為何被年輕世代拋棄

作者進一步指出，除了商戰消耗，年輕世代的集體背離是涼茶衰退的根本原因。核心消費群中選擇王老吉的比例已大幅腰斬，這主要源於兩大致命傷：第一是高糖含量與現代無糖健康風潮的劇烈衝突。一罐480毫升的王老吉含有約40克糖，相當於10塊方糖，在無糖茶與氣泡水大行其道的市場顯得格格不入，而品牌後續推出的無糖版又因中藥味過重且口感苦澀難獲好評；第二是消費場景嚴重受限，王老吉長久以來被綁定為吃麻辣鍋、燒烤解膩的「火鍋伴侶」或逢年過節的吉祥禮品，缺乏日常隨機解渴的高頻場景。在健康意識覺醒與替代品繁多的衝擊下，老牌涼茶正面臨被主流年輕市場邊緣化的嚴峻挑戰。

================================================

Speaking of. herbal tea, when was the last time you. drank a Wanglaoji? It’s been at least. a year or two for me. Looking back a. decade or so, how popular was this can. of herbal tea? Wanglaoji as their go-to thirst. quencher dropped from 43%in 2022 to 27%. in 2025. man named Wang Zebang sold herbal tea. on the street, and because he helped. cure many people during an epidemic, he. became famous. Later, after many twists and turns, it. became state-owned, with the trademark. belonging to the Guangzhou. Pharmaceutical Group. Note that it was. a paid lease for the usage rights; the. ownership still belonged to Guangzhou. Pharmaceutical. Back then, Wanglaoji. was just a regional brand with some. fame in Guangdong, with annual sales of. no more than tens of millions. Later,. Chen Hongdao hired a consulting firm. for positioning, and they came up with. that ad slogan that changed the Chinese. beverage industry: "Afraid of getting. internal heat? Drink Wanglaoji." What. made this slogan so brilliant? It. transformed a medicinal herbal drink. into a functional beverage for. preventing internal heat. Suddenly, the. target audience for the beverage. expanded significantly. Take Guangdong. for example; sore throats, hoarseness,. bad breath, insomnia—all these. symptoms could be attributed to " internal heat," a concept every Chinese. person understood. Eating hot pot,. staying up late, or eating barbecue. could all cause internal heat. So, are. you afraid of getting internal heat? Then just drink Wanglaoji; the target. audience instantly became over a. billion Chinese people. More. importantly, in the early 21 st-century. Chinese advertising market, TV ads were. still king. Wanglaoji seized the.

opportunity, spending a record-breaking. 420 million on ads in 2007 to become. the CCTV ad king, and the results were. immediate. In 2007, Wanglaoji's sales. were around 5 billion, and by 2008,. they had directly doubled, exceeding 10. billion. In 2010, the Wanglaoji. trademark was valued at 108 billion,. but just as Wanglaoji was at its peak,. a protracted trademark war broke out. Let's clarify the relationships first:. the owner of the Wanglaoji trademark is. the Guangzhou Pharmaceutical Group, but. there were two main products on the. market: the green-boxed Wanglaoji. managed by Guangzhou Pharmaceutical,. and the red-canned Wanglaoji, licensed. to the Hongdao Group, with JDB. responsible for production, sales,. distribution, and advertising. The. problem lay right there: in 2008, sales. of red-canned Wanglaoji exceeded 10. billion. How much did Guangzhou. Pharmaceutical receive in trademark. fees that year? About 5 million, which. is 0.05%of sales. According to. international standards, brand. licensing fees are 2%to 8%. Guangzhou. Pharmaceutical saw they were making so. much while they got so little, and they. definitely weren't having it. A bigger. bombshell was buried in the contract. term. The original trademark license. was set to expire in 2010. Later, both. parties signed a supplementary. agreement extending it to 2020. However. , the signing process involved bribery,. so Guangzhou Pharmaceutical argued it. wasn't compliant, the agreement was. invalid, and they wanted the trademark. back. JDB panicked, claiming they paid. for the agreement and had the right to. continue using it until 2020. The two. sides were deadlocked. In 2011,. Guangzhou Pharmaceutical filed for. arbitration, and the legal battle. officially began, lasting for several. years. There were three main points of. contention. First and most core: was.

the supplementary agreement actually. valid? This would determine whether JDB. could continue using the Wanglaoji. trademark. In July 2012, the court. ruled that JDB could no longer use the. Wanglaoji trademark. Helplessly, JDB. renamed its product JDB herbal tea. The. focus of the conflict shifted from the. trademark itself to who owned the. commercial value accumulated by. Wanglaoji in the past. Then came the. second dispute over advertising slogans. . After the name change, JDB's ad. slogan became, "The national sales. leader in herbal tea, now renamed JDB." But Wanglaoji wasn't having it, arguing. that the previous top-selling product. was called Wanglaoji and accusing JDB. of false advertising. This led to. another lawsuit. Starting in 2012, they. fought back and forth until the Supreme. Court finally ruled in 2019 that the. statement was factually accurate and. did not constitute false advertising. Finally, there was the dispute over. product packaging: who gets to use the. classic red can design? It dragged on. until a 2017 court ruling stated that. as long as it doesn't infringe on the. legal rights of others, both parties. can use it, so stop fighting. Some have. calculated that Wanglaoji and JDB have. fought dozens of lawsuits, with. compensation amounts ranging from. hundreds of millions to over a billion. yuan. Looking at market data, Wanglaoji. is deeper in the game. Figures show. that in 2023, the herbal tea market. reached about 45 billion yuan in sales,. with Wanglaoji accounting for 44%and. JDB for 25%. But do you think JDB is. the biggest loser? No, the one that. ended up worst off is actually the. third player, Heqizheng. Back in 2010,. Heqizheng's annual sales exceeded 2. billion yuan, firmly ranking second in. the industry, just behind Wanglaoji. But after Wanglaoji and JDB split, the. monopoly turned into a duopoly. As both.

sides scrambled frantically for. channels and shelf space, Heqizheng. ended up fading into obscurity. There. were no winners in this business war. that lasted over a decade. JDB lost its. original branding, and although. Wanglaoji regained its trademark, it's. hard to replicate its past glory. From. 2020 to 2023, sales dropped by 1. billion yuan in three years, and. compared to the 20 billion in 2012, it. has been cut in half. So the question. is, why don't young people like. drinking this herbal tea anymore? There. are three main reasons. First, the. sugar content is too high, running. counter to health trends. How much. sugar is in a 480ml can of Wanglaoji. herbal tea? About 40 grams. Since one. sugar cube is about 4 grams, that's. equivalent to 10 sugar cubes in one. bottle. Just look at the drinks in. convenience stores now. Oriental Leaf,. Suntory Oolong Tea, sparkling water—. they are all zero-sugar, zero-fat, and. zero-calorie. Wanglaoji's sugar content. just doesn't fit in anymore. To follow. the trend, my Wong Lo Kat also launched. a sugar-free herbal tea, but the. feedback has been quite polarized. Some. consumers complained that the. sugar-free version tastes bitter, the. medicinal flavor is too strong, and. it’s even more expensive. That’s. quite awkward. Adding sugar is. unhealthy, but not adding it makes it. taste too bad. Let’s talk about the " cooling" claim. Wong Lo Kat’s. ingredients include chrysanthemum,. honeysuckle, and licorice, which are. traditional Chinese medicines known for. clearing heat and detoxifying. But. don’t forget, it’s essentially a. drink packed with massive amounts of. sugar. Is it logical to rely on a. high-sugar drink to "cool down"? According to the simple belief in. Guangdong and Guangxi, the more bitter. something is, the better it clears heat.

. For instance, bitter melon or herbal. soup. If you have "internal heat," just. stop by any herbal tea shop with a. yellow sign on the street. There’s no. fire a bottle can’t put out; if there. is, just have two. The second biggest. reason herbal tea is being abandoned by. young people is the limited use case; it’s trapped as a "hot pot companion. " When do people actually buy Wong Lo. Kat? Usually when eating hot pot or. barbecue, or during holidays. The red. packaging is festive, and the name " Wong Lo Kat" implies good fortune. Gifting two boxes is both respectful. and affordable. Therefore, we see that. its sales have clear seasonal. fluctuations. The 2023 financial report. mentions this: sales grow when it’s. hot, and peak during major holidays. In. other words, summer sales rely on the. temperature, and winter sales rely on. gifting. The problem is that both. scenarios are being siphoned off by. other brands. With hot pot, you can. have plum juice, coconut milk, or soy. milk; Wong Lo Kat isn't a must-have. As. for gifts, there are more choices now. —milk, nuts, premium fruit—all. taking a slice of the pie. A third. reason fewer people drink Wong Lo Kat. is brand aging and a lack of product. innovation. Over the past decade, the. beverage market has changed drastically. . Zero-sugar, zero-calorie,. electrolyte-replenishing,. protein-packed, and energy-boosting. drinks are everywhere. In contrast,. Wong Lo Kat’s packaging and flavor. have basically remained unchanged. It’s not like Wong Lo Kat hasn’t. tried, but it seems the harder they try. , the more pathetic it gets. In 2025,. they sponsored "Keep Running 8," with a. reported sponsorship fee of 130 million. yuan, and became a super partner for " Singer 2026." They signed Zhang Linghe. one moment and announced Haaland the. next. The buzz was huge, but product.

sales barely budged. In 2025, Wong Lo. Kat's health division revenue was 8.786. billion yuan, a year-on-year increase. of only 0.23%. Wong Lo Kat has also. experimented with new flavors,. launching a whole series of quirky. flavors in recent years. Houttuynia,. durian—just hearing the names is. enough to feel shocked! But on social. media platforms, there are countless. complaints about these "dark cuisine" flavors, with some people even saying. the Houttuynia flavor tastes like a. urinal cleaning ball from a men's. restroom. After launching so many new. products, the one that still carries. the brand is that classic red can. In. fact, Wong Lo Kat's predicament is a. microcosm of the entire traditional. beverage industry. Over the past decade. , the Chinese beverage market has. undergone massive changes. The. sugar-free market has grown over. sevenfold, with Oriental Leaf. dominating. Meanwhile, functional. drinks are rising, topping 200 billion. yuan, and electrolyte water has become. a star product. As for herbal tea,. it’s not just Wong Lo Kat; the entire. category is hitting the brakes. Data. from the Forward Industry Research. Institute shows that the growth rate of. the tea market declined year by year. from 2012 to 2017. Looking back, Wong. Lo Kat and Jia Duo Bao fought for over. a decade, really just for a name, a red. can, and the consumer recognition built. up over the past. But while they were. fighting to the death, consumers had. already moved on, starting to ask: Why. should I still drink a can of. high-sugar herbal tea? This is the most. poignant aspect of the business world. You give your all and use every tactic. to outcompete your rival, only to look. up and realize the system has quietly. changed the map, turning your. once-lethal moves into nothing but air. Follow the trends, don't stay still.

Chen Hongdao hired a consulting firm. for positioning, and they came up with. that ad slogan that changed the Chinese. beverage industry: "Afraid of getting. internal heat? Drink Wanglaoji." What. made this slogan so brilliant? It. transformed a medicinal herbal drink. into a functional beverage for. preventing internal heat. Suddenly, the. target audience for the beverage. expanded significantly. Take Guangdong. for example; sore throats, hoarseness,. bad breath, insomnia—all these. symptoms could be attributed to " internal heat," a concept every Chinese. person understood. Eating hot pot,. staying up late, or eating barbecue. could all cause internal heat. So, are. you afraid of getting internal heat? Then just drink Wanglaoji; the target. audience instantly became over a. billion Chinese people. More. importantly, in the early 21 st-century. Chinese advertising market, TV ads were. still king. Wanglaoji seized the.

opportunity, spending a record-breaking. 420 million on ads in 2007 to become. the CCTV ad king, and the results were. immediate. In 2007, Wanglaoji's sales. were around 5 billion, and by 2008,. they had directly doubled, exceeding 10. billion. In 2010, the Wanglaoji. trademark was valued at 108 billion,. but just as Wanglaoji was at its peak,. a protracted trademark war broke out. Let's clarify the relationships first:. the owner of the Wanglaoji trademark is. the Guangzhou Pharmaceutical Group, but. there were two main products on the. market: the green-boxed Wanglaoji. managed by Guangzhou Pharmaceutical,. and the red-canned Wanglaoji, licensed. to the Hongdao Group, with JDB. responsible for production, sales,. distribution, and advertising. The. problem lay right there: in 2008, sales. of red-canned Wanglaoji exceeded 10. billion. How much did Guangzhou. Pharmaceutical receive in trademark. fees that year? About 5 million, which. is 0.05%of sales. According to. international standards, brand. licensing fees are 2%to 8%. Guangzhou. Pharmaceutical saw they were making so. much while they got so little, and they. definitely weren't having it. A bigger. bombshell was buried in the contract. term. The original trademark license. was set to expire in 2010. Later, both. parties signed a supplementary. agreement extending it to 2020. However. , the signing process involved bribery,. so Guangzhou Pharmaceutical argued it. wasn't compliant, the agreement was. invalid, and they wanted the trademark. back. JDB panicked, claiming they paid. for the agreement and had the right to. continue using it until 2020. The two. sides were deadlocked. In 2011,. Guangzhou Pharmaceutical filed for. arbitration, and the legal battle. officially began, lasting for several. years. There were three main points of. contention. First and most core: was.

the supplementary agreement actually. valid? This would determine whether JDB. could continue using the Wanglaoji. trademark. In July 2012, the court. ruled that JDB could no longer use the. Wanglaoji trademark. Helplessly, JDB. renamed its product JDB herbal tea. The. focus of the conflict shifted from the. trademark itself to who owned the. commercial value accumulated by. Wanglaoji in the past. Then came the. second dispute over advertising slogans. . After the name change, JDB's ad. slogan became, "The national sales. leader in herbal tea, now renamed JDB." But Wanglaoji wasn't having it, arguing. that the previous top-selling product. was called Wanglaoji and accusing JDB. of false advertising. This led to. another lawsuit. Starting in 2012, they. fought back and forth until the Supreme. Court finally ruled in 2019 that the. statement was factually accurate and. did not constitute false advertising. Finally, there was the dispute over. product packaging: who gets to use the. classic red can design? It dragged on. until a 2017 court ruling stated that. as long as it doesn't infringe on the. legal rights of others, both parties. can use it, so stop fighting. Some have. calculated that Wanglaoji and JDB have. fought dozens of lawsuits, with. compensation amounts ranging from. hundreds of millions to over a billion. yuan. Looking at market data, Wanglaoji. is deeper in the game. Figures show. that in 2023, the herbal tea market. reached about 45 billion yuan in sales,. with Wanglaoji accounting for 44%and. JDB for 25%. But do you think JDB is. the biggest loser? No, the one that. ended up worst off is actually the. third player, Heqizheng. Back in 2010,. Heqizheng's annual sales exceeded 2. billion yuan, firmly ranking second in. the industry, just behind Wanglaoji. But after Wanglaoji and JDB split, the. monopoly turned into a duopoly. As both.

sides scrambled frantically for. channels and shelf space, Heqizheng. ended up fading into obscurity. There. were no winners in this business war. that lasted over a decade. JDB lost its. original branding, and although. Wanglaoji regained its trademark, it's. hard to replicate its past glory. How much. sugar is in a 480ml can of Wanglaoji. herbal tea? About 40 grams. Since one. sugar cube is about 4 grams, that's. equivalent to 10 sugar cubes in one. bottle. Wanglaoji's sugar content. just doesn't fit in anymore. To follow. the trend, my Wong Lo Kat also launched. a sugar-free herbal tea, but the. feedback has been quite polarized. Adding sugar is. unhealthy, but not adding it makes it. taste too bad. Let’s talk about the " cooling" claim. Wong Lo Kat’s. ingredients include chrysanthemum,. honeysuckle, and licorice, which are. traditional Chinese medicines known for. clearing heat and detoxifying. But. don’t forget, it’s essentially a. drink packed with massive amounts of. sugar. Is it logical to rely on a. high-sugar drink to "cool down"? According to the simple belief in. Guangdong and Guangxi, the more bitter. something is, the better it clears heat.

. For instance, bitter melon or herbal. soup. If you have "internal heat," just. stop by any herbal tea shop with a. yellow sign on the street. There’s no. fire a bottle can’t put out; if there. is, just have two. The second biggest. reason herbal tea is being abandoned by. young people is the limited use case; it’s trapped as a "hot pot companion. " When do people actually buy Wong Lo. Kat? Usually when eating hot pot or. barbecue, or during holidays. The red. packaging is festive, and the name " Wong Lo Kat" implies good fortune. Gifting two boxes is both respectful. and affordable. Therefore, we see that. its sales have clear seasonal. fluctuations. The 2023 financial report. mentions this: sales grow when it’s. hot, and peak during major holidays. In. other words, summer sales rely on the. temperature, and winter sales rely on. gifting. The problem is that both. scenarios are being siphoned off by. other brands. With hot pot, you can. have plum juice, coconut milk, or soy. milk; Wong Lo Kat isn't a must-have. As. for gifts, there are more choices now. —milk, nuts, premium fruit—all. taking a slice of the pie. A third. reason fewer people drink Wong Lo Kat. is brand aging and a lack of product. innovation. Over the past decade, the. beverage market has changed drastically. . Zero-sugar, zero-calorie,. electrolyte-replenishing,. protein-packed, and energy-boosting. drinks are everywhere. In contrast,. Wong Lo Kat’s packaging and flavor. have basically remained unchanged. It’s not like Wong Lo Kat hasn’t. tried, but it seems the harder they try. , the more pathetic it gets. In 2025,. they sponsored "Keep Running 8," with a. reported sponsorship fee of 130 million. yuan, and became a super partner for " Singer 2026." sales barely budged. In 2025, Wong Lo. Kat's health division revenue was 8.786. billion yuan, a year-on-year increase. of only 0.23%. But on social. media platforms, there are countless. complaints about these "dark cuisine" flavors, with some people even saying. the Houttuynia flavor tastes like a. urinal cleaning ball from a men's. restroom. After launching so many new. products, the one that still carries. the brand is that classic red can. In. fact, Wong Lo Kat's predicament is a. microcosm of the entire traditional. beverage industry. Over the past decade. , the Chinese beverage market has. undergone massive changes. The. sugar-free market has grown over. sevenfold, with Oriental Leaf. dominating. Meanwhile, functional. drinks are rising, topping 200 billion. yuan, and electrolyte water has become. a star product. As for herbal tea,. it’s not just Wong Lo Kat; the entire. category is hitting the brakes. Data. from the Forward Industry Research. Institute shows that the growth rate of. the tea market declined year by year. from 2012 to 2017. Looking back, Wong. Lo Kat and Jia Duo Bao fought for over. a decade, really just for a name, a red. can, and the consumer recognition built. up over the past. Follow the trends, don't stay still.

  • 全面還原王老吉與加多寶長達十餘年的世紀商標訴訟大戰，揭示巨頭內耗如何徹底改變中國涼茶產業格局。
  • 剖析Z世代年輕族群的消費心理與無糖健康趨勢，探討傳統功能性飲料受限於特定場景的生存困境。

摘要

昔日國民神飲：從嶺南草藥到百億傳奇

作者指出，曾被譽為「國民涼茶」的王老吉在2012年年銷售額一度突破200億元人民幣，相當於全國每人每年喝掉四罐，甚至創下市場上每賣出十罐涼茶就有七罐是王老吉的驚人紀錄。回溯歷史，該品牌起源於清代道光年間廣州名醫王澤邦在街頭售賣的草藥茶，歷經歷史變遷後成為廣藥集團旗下的國有資產。真正將王老吉推向全國的關鍵人物，是後來創立加多寶集團的陳鴻道。他在1995年租賃了商標使用權，並透過定位諮詢提煉出顛覆性的廣告詞「怕上火，喝王老吉」，成功將具有嶺南地域特色的藥性飲品轉型為預防上火的功能性飲料。配合2007年豪擲4.2億元奪得央視廣告標王，王老吉銷量瞬間暴增，於2010年商標估值高達1080億元。

兩虎相爭無贏家：十餘年的世紀商標內耗

健康風潮與場景禁錮：涼茶為何被年輕世代拋棄

作者進一步指出，除了商戰消耗，年輕世代的集體背離是涼茶衰退的根本原因。核心消費群中選擇王老吉的比例已大幅腰斬，這主要源於兩大致命傷：第一是高糖含量與現代無糖健康風潮的劇烈衝突。一罐480毫升的王老吉含有約40克糖，相當於10塊方糖，在無糖茶與氣泡水大行其道的市場顯得格格不入，而品牌後續推出的無糖版又因中藥味過重且口感苦澀難獲好評；第二是消費場景嚴重受限，王老吉長久以來被綁定為吃麻辣鍋、燒烤解膩的「火鍋伴侶」或逢年過節的吉祥禮品，缺乏日常隨機解渴的高頻場景。在健康意識覺醒與替代品繁多的衝擊下，老牌涼茶正面臨被主流年輕市場邊緣化的嚴峻挑戰。
